instruction.text: Read the chapter, then answer the reading comprehension questions.

atoms.text: Jake makes the same face at me this morning as he does every morning; his nose wrinkles up and his eyes fill with annoyance. Each school day he gets on the bus and makes a big show so that everyone knows that the seat next to me is the last one he would choose. It’s the same in class. He makes sure everyone knows that he isn’t sitting next to me by choice and that we are definitely NOT friends. I know he feels unlucky to have to sit next to me. I would feel unlucky if I were Jake, too.

atoms.text: I hate school. Nobody wants to talk to me, let alone be my friend. I spend most of my time trying to avoid my classmates and teachers. Nothing good ever happens when I try to talk to people.

Today is no different from any other day. Jake talks to the girls and all three of them ignore me. Mrs Bailey calls on me and I pretend not to have the answer. I hate answering questions. I usually have the right answer in my head, but I don’t want to be wrong in front of everyone. During break, I sit on my swing and enjoy being outside. I don’t like sports too much any more because I feel like everyone is judging how bad I am and that I ruin the game for people. I used to play football, but then mum died, and I stopped.

Finally, school is over, and I can go home. Now that mum’s gone, I live with my grandma. I love my grandma, but she’s getting forgetful. As I walk through the door, I hear the Quiz Show playing. She loves that. She calls out all the answers and celebrates every time, even when she is dead wrong. I wonder if she can still read the answers on the screen. Rufus, my favourite dog in the world, sits next to her. He used to be my mum’s dog, but now he’s mine. He’s always happy to see me and wags his tail and greets me at the door and slobbers on me. I don’t mind though.

In my room, I drop off my backpack and lay down on my bed, where Rufus joins me. I open my comic book to the spot from last night and continue to read until I’m bored. When I get hungry, I make dinner. We’re lucky. Since Grandma has been so sick, she’s been enrolled in a program that delivers food to us. Grabbing the mac and cheese, I make enough for both of us. Later, I take Rufus, and we make our way to my favourite spot. On the way there, Rufus hops in the stream and then on me. I am a bit muddy and wet, but I don’t mind. We sit on a rock together and wait for the sun to go down before walking back home.

atoms.a: Who is the narrator in this chapter and what narrative style is it told in?
Why does Norbert hate answering questions?
b: He never has the correct answer and thinks he’s stupid.
He doesn’t hate it at all. He answers questions all the time.
++He does not want to be wrong in front of the other kids.

atoms.a: What do you learn at the end of the third paragraph?
b: Norbert sits on the swing during break.
Norbert doesn’t like playing football any more.

atoms.a: Select the correct answer about Norbert’s grandmother.
b: Norbert’s grandmother is very healthy and active and helps him walk Rufus every day.
Norbert’s grandmother is frustrated with him and tells him to play sports and participate more.
++Norbert’s grandmother is his guardian, but she is not able to help him with many things.
